::: {.why}
Every strategy that stopped working looks like a regime change afterwards, and a model that can declare regimes will always find them, so the discipline is in the out-of-sample test rather than in the fit.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Fit a two-state Markov switching model and interpret the transition matrix in terms of expected regime duration.
- Say what a regime model can and cannot do in real time, and why the smoothed state probabilities are not usable for trading.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Fit a two-state Markov switching model to your spread or to index returns with statsmodels, and report the transition matrix, the implied expected duration of each state, and the state-conditional parameters.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Make the distinction that matters: plot the smoothed state probabilities against the filtered ones. The smoothed series uses future data and looks convincing; the filtered series is what you would have had. Then run a changepoint detection on the same series with ruptures and compare where the two methods put the breaks.
:::
:::
